The present sciences are the daughters of mysterious sciences from which rorig;ine is lost in the night of time, Valchimie is the mother of chemistry, Vastrolog;ie preceded astronomy, at the basis of mathematics one finds the cabal and qualitative geometry, in the principle history merges with mythology, medicine was taught to men by a god. You only know a science when you know its history. From the vide mother who founded science to the present day, what unceasing efforts, what trial and error! We profit from the labors of our predecessors, carelessly, without thinking of the enormous amount of physical and intellectual labor they have expended to pave the way for us. Many have spent their lives, spent their fortunes, renounced pleasures and honors for the sake of science. How many martyrs have died affirming to the last breath the eternal truth! It is Roger Bacon, persecuted all his life by ignorant monks, it is the learned Hypatia stoned by the

It is Bernard the Trevisan who is hated and tormented by his angry parents to see him spend his fortune in alchemical researches, it is Denis Zaccharius murdered by his cousin to whom he had refused to reveal the secret of the philosopher's stone, it is Cardan, poor of their whole life. To do justice to these great men by bringing their works back to light, by reviving them in their works, has been our goal. However, their works have become scarce, large libraries alone could provide researchers with sufficient documents, but it is known how difficult it is to obtain permission to work in a public library. On the other hand, to form a private collection is very expensive and requires time and patience, often one finds only after several years of research the work one desires; finally most of these treatises are written in barbaric Latin, of an obscure style very tiring to read. All these reasons prompted us to publish these translations. The authors have been carefully chosen from among the greatest names in alchemy: Arnauld de Villeneuve, Raymond Lulle le Docteur Illuminée, Albert le Grand,

VII mixing everything in his vast erudition, Roger ' Bacon the admirable doctor, anticipating his century and substituting experience and observation for the hollow ramblings of scholastics, finally Paracelsus, the great Paracelsus, upsetting the old theories, combining alchemy with medicine, never had a greater influence on his century. We took the most important treaties, four out of five are translated into French for the first time. As for the translation, it is as accurate as possible, the obscure passages are rendered word for word; we have endeavoured to give the sentence the turn it has in the text. Finally, the treatises are preceded by a biographical note and a bibliographic index. y We conclude with a piece of advice: to read this book without being prepared is to expose oneself not to understand it, so one will do well before reading: “Alchemy and the Alchemists” of M. sections.h: NOTICE ON THE EMERALD TABLE OF HERMÈS
p: The Emerald table of Hermes Trismegistus, the Egyptian High is the cornerstone of alchemy. Philosophers quote it at all times, so it is important to know this document. It is found in all important collections of hermetic treatises: iheatrum chemicuin, Bibliotheca chemica maneli, Bibliolheca conlracta Albinei, Library of Alchemical Philosophers of Salmon, etc. The following translation is that of the Library of Alchemical Philosophers of Salmon revised and corrected from the Latin text at the head of the Bibliotheca chemica contracta Albinei.

It is true, without a lie, certain and very true. That which is below is like that which is above, and that which is above is like that which is below, to perform the miracles of one thing only. This Mercury is the first of all metals. I shall further teach how to make this transmutation, thus destroying the opinion of those who claim that the form of metals cannot be changed. They would be right if metals could not be reduced to their raw material, but I will show that this reduction to the raw material is easy and that transmutation is possible and feasible. For everything that is born, everything that grows, multiplies according to its kind, so trees, men, herbs. One seed can produce a thousand other seeds. So it is possible to multiply things to infinity. From the foregoing, he who analyzes things will see that if the Philosophers have spoken in an obscure manner, they have at least spoken the truth. They said that our Stone has a soul, a body and a spirit, which is true. They have compared his imperfect body to the body, because it is powerless in itself; they have called the Water a vital spirit, because it gives the body, imperfect in itself and inert, the life it did not have before and perfects its form. They have called the soul leaver, for as will be seen later, he has also given life to the imperfect body, perfecting it and changing it into his own nature.

The philosopher says, “Change natures and you will find what you are looking for. “That is true. For in our Magisterium we draw first the subtle from the thick, the spirit from the body, and finally the dry from the wet, that is to say, the land of Water, thus we change the natures that which was below, we put it above; so that the spirit becomes body, then the body becomes spirit. Philosophers still say that we make our Stone from one thing and with one vessel and they are right. All our magisterium is drawn from; our Water and is made with it. It dissolves the metals themselves, but it is not by changing into the water of the cloud, as the ignorant believe. It calcifies and reduces to earth. It transforms the bodies into ashes, it incinerates, whitens and cleans, as Morien says; “The Azoth and the fire cleanse the Brass, that is, wash it and completely remove its blackness. “Brass is an impure body, azoth is silver. Our Water unites different bodies together, if they have been prepared as it has just been said; this union is such that neither fire nor any other force can separate them by the combustion of their igneous principle. This transmutation steals the bodies, but this is not the vulgar sublimation of the simple-minded, of people without experience, for whom to sublimate is to elevate. These people take charred bodies, mix them with sublimable spirits, that is to say mercury, arsenic, sulfur etc. , and they sublimate it all with the help of a strong heat. Burned bodies are driven by spirits and they say they are sublimated. But what is their disappointment when they find unclean bodies with their spirits more unclean than before! Our sublation does not consist in raising the sublimation of the Philosophers; phes is an operation that makes a vile and corrupt thing (by the earth) another thing purer. In the same way, when it is commonly said that such a one has been raised to the episcopate... “High” means that he has been exalted and placed in a more honorable position. In the same way we say that bodies have changed in nature, that is to say that they have been exalted, that their essence has become purer, so we see that to sublimate is the same thing; that to purify is what our Water does. ; This is how we must hear our philosophical sublimation on which many have been mistaken. Now our Water mortifies, illumines, cleanses and vivifies; it first makes the black colors appear during the

mortification of the body, then come many and varied colors, and finally whiteness. In the mixture of the water and the ferment of the body, that is to say of the prepared body, an infinity of colors appear. This is how our Magisterium is drawn from one, is made with one, and it consists of four and three are in one. Learn again, Venerable Father, that the philosophers have multiplied the names of the Mixed Stone for the better. They have said that it is corporeal and spiritual, and they have not lied, the Sages will understand. For it has a spirit and a body; the body is spiritual only in the solution, and the spirit has become corporeal by its union with the body. Some call it closure, others call it airain. Morien says: “The knowledge of our Magisterium is comparable in all things to the procreation of the Tiomme. First, the coitus. Second, the design. Third, the imbiblity. Fourth, the birth. Fifth, nutrition or diet. “I will explain these words to you. Our sperm, which is Mercury, unites with the earth, that is to say, with the imperfect body, also called Mother Earth (the earth being the mother of all the elements). This is what we mean by coitus. Then when the earth has retained within itself a little bit of Mercury, it is said to be illyaconception. When we say that the male acts on the female, we must understand by this that Mercury acts on the earth. This is why the Philosophers have said that our Magisterium is male and female and that it results from the union of these two principles. After the addition of Water, that is, Mercury, the earth grows and increases by whitening, it is then said that ilyaimbition. Then the ferment coagulates, that is to say, it joins the imperfect body, prepared as it has been said, until its color and appearance are uniform, it is the birth, because at this moment appears our Stone which the Philosophers have called: the King, as it is said in the Peat: “Honor our King coming forth from the fire, crowned with a great crown of gold, that the crown be obeyed. His father is the Sun, his mother is the Moon; the Moon is the imperfect body. The Sun is the perfect body. Fifthly and lastly comes food, the more it is nourished, the more it grows. Now, Lise feeds on her milk, that is, on the sperm that gave birth to her in the beginning. It must therefore be soaked in Mercury, until it has drunk two parts of it, or more if necessary.

Now comes the practice. Now let’s move on to practice, as I mentioned above. And first all bodies must be brought back to the raw material to make transmutation possible. I will show you everything that has been said above. Therefore, my son, I beg you not to disdain my practice, because in it is hidden all our Magisterium, as I have seen in my occult faith. Take a pound of gold, reduce it to very bright filings, mix it with four parts of our purified water, grinding it and incorporating it with a little salt and vinegar, until the whole is amalgamated. The gold, therefore, having been well amalgamated, put it in a great quantity of Eau-de-vle, that is to say, of Mercury, and put it all in r Urinai on our purified center; make it below one; very slow fire for a whole day; then let it cool, and when it is cold, take the Water and all that is with it, filter it through a linen cloth, until it has passed. Set aside what remains on the linen, collect it and having put it in a new quantity of Holy Water in the

This done, take all this Water, put it in a glass vase and cook it slowly until you see the darkness appear on its surface you will remove the black patches with skill. Continue until the whole body is changed into pure earth. The more you do this, the better it will be. Recline then, removing the darkness, until the darkness is gone, and the Water, that is, our Mercury, appears bright. Then take all this earth, that is to say, the darkness that you have gathered, put it in a vessel of glass, pour over the Blessed Water, so that nothing goes beyond the surface of the water, and nothing floats; and heat it with light fire for ten days, and then grind it, and so add again the new water, and add again the new water. Cook at last with violent fire always in the same vessel, until the earth becomes white and brilliant. Having therefore bleached and coagulated our land, take

The water of life which has been thickened with a slight heat by the coagulated earth, cook it at a violent fire in a good cucurbit with its capital, until all that ilyad’Eau in the mixture has passed into the container and the calcined earth remains in the cucurbit. Take then three parts for four of a ferment, that is to say, if you have taken one pound of the imperfect body or of gold, you will take three pounds of ferment, that is to say, of the Sun or of the Moon. You will first have to dissolve this ferment, reduce it to earth and repeat in a word the same operations as for the imperfect body. Only then will you unite them, soak them with the water that has passed through the vessel, and bake for three days or more. Imbibede again, recuis and repeat this operation until these two bodies remain united, that is to say, become one. You'll weigh. Their color will not have changed. Then you will pour out on them the water already named, little by little, until they no longer absorb it. In this union of bodies, the Spirit is incorporated into them and as they have been purified, it changes into their own nature. This is how the germ is transformed in the purified bodies, which would not have happened before because of their coarseness and impurities. The mind grows in them, it increases and multiplies.

RECAPITULATION. Now, venerable Father, I will return to what I have said by applying it to the preparations of the ancient Philosophers and to their teachings so obscure, so incomprehensible. Yet weigh the words of the Philosophers, you will understand and confess that they have spoken the truth. The first word of our Magisterium or of the Work is the reduction of Mercury (the body), that is, the reduction of copper or another metal into Mercury. This is what the Philosophers call the solution, which is the foundation of Art, as Franciscus says: “If you do not dissolve the bodies, you work in vain. This is the solution of which Parmenides speaks in the Peat of the Philosophers. Upon hearing the word solution, the ignorant immediately think of the Water of the Clouds. But if they had read our books, if they had understood them, they would know that our Water is permanent, and that separated from its body it becomes therefore immutable. So the solution of the Philosophers is not the water of the cloud, but the conversion of bodies into water from which they were first procreated, that is, into water.

Mercury. In the same way, the ice changes into the water that had first given it birth. Here, then, by the grace of God you know the first element which is Water and the reduction of this same body into the raw material. The second word is “What is made of the earth.” That's what the Philosophers said. “Water comes out of the earth. You will have the second element, which is the earth. The third word of the Philosophers is the purification of the Stone. Morien says about this: “This Water rots and purifies itself with the earth, etc. The Philosopher said, “United with the wet cr, the dry is the earth; the wet is the water. You will already have the water and the earth in itself and the whitened earth with the water. The fourth word is that Water can evaporate through sublimation or ascension. It becomes air again by separating from the earth with which it was previously coagulated and joined and thus you will have the Earth, the Air; and the Water. This is what the Philosopher says in the Peat: K Whiten it and sublimate it with a sharp fire until there escapes a spirit which is Mercury. This is why it is called Hermès bird and Hermogene chicken. You will find at the bottom a charred earth, it is an igneous force, that is to say of an igneous nature.

So you will have the four elements, the earth, the fire and this charred earth, which is the powder of which Morien speaks” (Do not despise the powder that is at the bottom because it is in a low place). It is the earth of the body, it is your sperm and in it is the coronation of the Work. Then with the above earth settles the ferment, that ferment which the Philosophers call the soul: and here is why: just as the body of man is nothing without his soul, so the dead earth or filthy body is nothing without its ferment, that is, without his soul. For the ferment prepares the imperfect body, changes it into its own nature as it has been said. There are no ferments other than the Sun and the Moon, these two neighboring planets coming closer by their natural properties. This is what makes Morien say: “If you do not wash, if you do not whiten the filthy body and give it no soul, you will have done nothing for the Magisterium. The spirit is then united to the soul and the body, he rejoices with them and fixes himself. The water changes, and what was thick becomes subtle. This is what Astanus says in the Philosophers’ Peat: “The mind does not join the bodies until they have been perfectly cleansed of their impurities. In this union appear the greatest miracles.

For all imaginable colours are then shown, and the imperfect body takes, according to Barsen, the colour of the ferment, while the ferment itself remains unaltered. O Father full of piety, may God increase in you the spirit of understanding so that you may weigh well what I am about to say: the elements can only be generated by their own sperm. This sperm is Mercury. Consider the man who can only be begotten with the help of sperm, the plants that can only be born with a seed, as much as is necessary for generation and growth. There are some who think they are doing the best, sublimating Mercury, fixing it, uniting it with other bodies, and yet they find nothing. Here is why: a sperm can change me, it remains as it was and it only produces its effect when it is worn in the womb of the woman. This is why the Philosopher Mechardus says: “If our Stone is not put into the womb of the female, in order to be nourished there, it will not increase. O Father, behold, you are in possession of the Stone of the Philosophers according to your desire. Glory to God. Here ends the little treatise of ArnauId de Villeneuve, given to the Pope, Benedict XI, in the year 1303.

Raymond Luile was born in Palma, Majorca, in 1235. His father, Seneschal de Jacques!" of Aragon, destined him for the career of arms. The youth of R. He was turbulent and licentious, the marriage did not change his conduct, but following a violent love ended in an unfortunate way, he renounced the world and after dividing his possessions among his children, he retired into solitude. It is then that he forms the project of converting the infidels, this will be the great idea to which he will devote his whole life. To learn Arabic, he buys a Muslim slave, but the latter having guessed the purpose of his master, tries to assassinate him. Raymond Luile founded a monastery where Arabic was taught and missionaries were trained. Then he travels Europe addressing popes, kings, emperors, asking some for their moral authority, others for help in money to make his work fruitful. It was in these peregrinations that he established relations in Paris with Arnauld de 'Villeneuve and Duns Scot. He visits Spain, Italy, France, Austria. Joining the example to the word, he passes twice in Africa, is sentenced to death in Tunis, and escapes only thanks to the

sections.h: THE COLLARBONE OF RAYMOND LULLE DE MAJORQUE
p: A treatise also known as the Universal Key, in which one will find clearly indicated all that is necessary to perfect the Great Work. We have called this work Clavicle, because without it it is impossible to understand our other books, the whole of which embraces the whole of Art, for our words are obscure to the ignorant. I have made many treatises, very extensive, but divided and obscure, as can be seen from the Testament, where I speak of the principles of nature and of all that pertains to art, but the text has been subjected to the hammer of Philosophy. The same for pou. * my book of the Mercury of the Philosophers, in the second chapter: of the fecundity of the physical miners, as well as my book of the Quintessence of Gold and Silver, as well as all my other works in which art is treated in a complete manner, except that I have always hidden the main secret. Now, without this secret no one can enter into the mines of philosophers and do anything useful; therefore, with the help and permission of the Most High, to whom I have been pleased to reveal the Great Work, I shall treat here of Art without any fiction. But beware of revealing this secret to the wicked; communicate it only to your intimate friends, though you must not reveal it to anyone, because it is a gift from God that makes it present to whom it seems good to him. Whoever owns it will have an eternal treasure. Learn to purify the perfect by the imperfect. The Sun is the father of all metals and the Moon is their mother, although the Moon receives its light from the Sun. From these two planets depends the entire magisterium. According to Avicenna, metals can only be transmuted after being returned to their raw material, which is true. You will first have to reduce metals to Mercury; but I do not mean here vulgar, volatile mercury, I am speaking of fixed Mercury; for vulgar mercury is volatile, full of a phlegmatic coldness, it is indispensable that it be reduced by fixed Mercury, hotter, drier, endowed with qualities contrary to those of vulgar mercury. That is why I advise you, my friends, not to operate on the Sun and the Moon until you have

They were brought to their raw material, which is the sulfur and Mercury of the philosophers. O my children, learn to make use of this venerable matter, for I warn you of it under oath, if you do not draw Mercury from these two metals, you will work like blind people, in darkness and in doubt. Therefore, my sons, I beseech you to walk towards the light, with your eyes open and not to fall blind into the abyss of perdition.

sections.h: CHAPTER I DIFFERENCES BETWEEN VULGAR MERCURY AND MERCURY
p: PHYSICS. We say: Vulgar Mercury cannot be the Mercury of the Philosophers, by any artifice that has been prepared for it, for Vulgar Mercury cannot hold on to fire; only with the help of a foreign corporeal Mercury that is hot, dry, and more digested than it. That is why I disk our physical Mercury is of a warmer and more fixed nature than vulgar mercury. Our corporeal mercury is converted into flowing mercury, not wetting the fingers; when it is joined with vulgar mercury, they unite and join so well with the help of a bond of love, that it is impossible to separate them from each other, in the same way from water mixed with water. This is the law of nature. Our Mercury penetrates the vulgar mercury and mixes with it by drying its phlegmatic moisture, removing its coldness, which makes it black as coal and finally makes it fall to dust. Note that vulgar mercury cannot be used in place of our physical Mercury, which possesses natural heat to the desired degree; even for this reason our Mercury communicates its own nature to vulgar mercury. Moreover, our Mercury, after its transmutation, changes the metals into pure metal, that is to say into Sun and Moon, as we have demonstrated in the second part of our Practice. But he does something even more remarkable, he changes vulgar mercury into medicine that can transmute imperfect metals into perfect. It changes the vulgar mercury into the true Sun and Moon, better than those that come out of the mine. Note again that our physical Mercury can transmute a hundred marks and more, to infinity, all of it.

of ordinary mercury, unless there is a shortage of it. I also want you to know something else, Mercury does not mix easily and never perfectly with other bodies, unless they have previously been brought back to its natural species. Therefore, when you wish to unite Mercury with the Sun or the Moon of the vulgar, you must first bring these metals back to their natural species, which is ordinary mercury, that with the help of the natural bond of love, then the male unites with the female. ; So our Mercury is active, hot and dry, while the vulgar Mercury is cold, moist, passive like the female which is held at home in a temperate heat until the obfuscation. Then these two mercurys turn black as coal; that is the secret of true dissolution. Then they join together in such a way that it becomes impossible to separate them ever. They then come in the form of a very white powder, and they beget male and female children by the true bond of love. These children will multiply infinitely according to their species because of an ounce of this powder, which can be projected, elixir white or red, you will make Suns in infinite number and you will transmute into the Moon all kind of metal emerged from a mine.

EXTRACTION OF MERCURY FROM THE PERFECT BODY. Take an ounce of cut-off moon lime, calcinela as described at the end of our work on the Magisterium. The lime will then be reduced to a fine powder on a porphyry plate. You will soak this powder, two, three, four times a day with good tartar oil prepared in the manner described at the end of this work and then you will dry in the sun. You will tingle until the lime has absorbed four or five parts of oil, the amount of lime being taken for a unit, you will spray the powder on the porphyry, as it has been said, after having dried it, for then it is more easily reduced to powder. When it has been well porphyrized, it will be inserted into a long-necked matras. You will add to it our stinking menstruation made with two parts of red vitriol and a part of saltpeter you will have previously distilled this mens-; trae seven times and you will have rectified it well by separating it from its earthy impurities, so that in the end this menstruation is completely essential.

Then we will read the matras perfectly, we will put it in the ash fire, with some coals, until we see the matter boil and dissolve. Finally, we will distill on the ashes until all the menstruation has passed and we will wait for the matter to be cold. When the vase is completely cooled, it will be opened, and the material will be placed in another very clean vase with its perfectly luteous capital. We'll put it all on ashes in a furnace. The lute being dry, it will first be gently heated until all the water of the material on which one operates has passed into the container. Then the fire is increased to completely dry out the matter and exalt the stinking spirits that will pass into the marquee and from there into the container. When you see the operation happen- at this point, you will let the ship cool down by gradually decreasing the fire. The vase being cold, you will remove the material that you will reduce to a subtle powder on the porphyry. You will put the impalpable powder thus obtained in a well-cooked and well-vitrified earthenware vessel. Then you will pour on top of it ordinary boiling water, stirring with a clean stick, until the mixture is thick as mustard. Stir well with the wand until you see a few globules of merFIVE TREATMENTS of aLChimie cure in the matter; there will soon be a rather large quantity according to what you will have used of the perfect body, that is to say of the Moon. And until you have a large quantity, pour boiling water from time to time and stir until all the matter is reduced to a body like vulgar mercury. We will remove the earthy impurities with cold water, we will dry on a cloth, we will pass through a chamois skin. And then you will see wonderful things.”

Take three large pieces of pure moon in tenuous slats; make an amalgam of them with four large pieces of well-washed vulgar mercury. When the amalgam is done you will put it in a small batras having a neck of one and a half feet. Then take our Mercury extracted above from the lunar body, and put it on the amalgam made with the

perfect body and vulgar mercury read the vase with; the best read possible and dry. This done, shake the matras strongly to mix the amalgam and the mercury well. Then place the vase where the matter is in a small furnace on a fire of a few coals only the heat of the fire must not be greater; than that of the sun when it is in the sign of the lion. Stronger heat would destroy your matter as conti; harm this degree of fire until the matter becomes as black as coal and as thick as porridge. Roger Bacon was born in 1214 in Ilcester, Sommerset County. He studied first at Oxford, and then came to Paris to take the titles of Master of Arts and Doctor of Theology. At that time, Albert the Great publicly professed in Paris. Returning to England, he entered the Order of the Franciscans around 1240. He learned Greek, Arabic, Hebrew to read the ancient authors in the text. He acquired a prodigious erudition. He returned to Paris, which offered him more facilities for his studies. His ignorant superiors, afraid of his knowledge, began to persecute him. Clement IV, who admired him, was powerless to protect him, and Bacon had to hide from his superiors to write and send Opus majus to the pope. Nicholas III succeeded Clement IV. It was under this pontiff that Jerome d’Esculo, general of the Franciscans, passing through Paris, had Roger Bacon locked up, accusing him of magic and heresy. Jerome d’Esculo was himself elected pope under the name of Nicholas IV, and Roger Bacon despaired of ever leaving his dungeon when he was

p: PREFACE. In their writings the Philosophers have expressed themselves in many different ways – but always enigmatic. They have bequeathed to us a noble science among all, but veiled completely for us by their cloudy word, entirely hidden under an impenetrable veil. And yet, they were right to do so. Therefore, I beseech you to exercise your mind with perseverance on these seven chapters, which contain the art of transmuting metals, without having to worry about the writings of other philosophers. Go back often in your mind to their beginning, their middle, their end, and you will find in them inventions so subtle that your soul will be filled with joy.
FIVE TREATISES OF ALCH1M;E

DEFINITIONS OF ALCHEMY. In some ancient manuscripts, there are several definitions of this art that we should talk about here. Hermes says, “Alchemy is the immutable science which works on bodies by means of theory and experience, and which, by a natural conjunction, transforms them into a higher, more precious species. Another philosopher said: “Alchemy teaches to transmute every kind of metal into another, with the aid of a particular Medicine, as can be seen from the many writings of the Philosophers. “Alchemy is the science that teaches to prepare a certain medicine or elixir, which being projected on imperfect metals, gives them perfection in the very moment of projection.
The Mirror of Alchemy

THE NATURAL PRINCIPLES AND THE GENERATION OF METALS, I will talk here about natural principles and the generation of metals. Note first that the principles of metals are Mercury and Sulfur. These two principles gave birth to all metals and minerals, of which there are many different species. I say moreover that nature has always had as its goal and is constantly striving to arrive at perfection, at gold. But as a result of various accidents that hinder its progress, metallic varieties are born, as it is clearly exposed in several philosophers. According to the purity or impurity of the two constituent principles, that is, Sulphur and Mercury, perfect or imperfect metals, gold, silver, tin, lead, copper, iron, are produced. Now piously collect these teachings on the nature of metals, on their purity or impurity, their poverty or their richness in principles.
FIVE TREATISES OF ALCHEMY

Nature of Gold: Gold is a perfect body composed of a pure Mercury, fixed, bright, red and a pure Sulfur, fixed, red, non-combustible. Gold is perfect. Nature of Silver: it is a pure, almost perfect body, composed of a pure Mercury, almost fixed, brilliant, white. Its sulfur has the same qualities. Silver lacks only a little more fixity, color and weight. Nature of tin; it is a pure, imperfect body, composed of a pure, fixed and volatile Mercury, bright, white on the outside, red on the inside. Its sulfur has the same qualities. It only lacks the tin to be a little more cooked and digested. Nature of lead: it is an impure and imperfect body, composed of an impure Mercury, unstable, terrestrial, powdery, slightly white on the outside, red on the inside. His smile is similar and more combustible. It lacks lead, purity, fixity, color; it is not cooked enough. Copper is an impure and imperfect metal, composed of an impure, unstable, terrestrial, combustible, red, non-splintered Mercury. The same goes for its sulfur. Copper lacks fixity, purity, weight. It contains too much impure color and incombustible earthy parts.
The Mirror of Alchemy

Iron is an impure, imperfect body, composed of an impure Mercury, too fixed, containing combustible earthy parts, white and red, but without brilliance. It lacks fusibility, purity, weight; it contains too much impure fixed sulfur and combustible earthy parts. Every alchemist must take into account the above.

Be careful, then; for if you have exercised the subtlety and sharpness of your mind over those chapters in which I have manifestly revealed to you the knowledge of Matter, you now possess that ineffable and delectable thing, the object of all the desires of the Philosophers.

SHIP AND STOVE. We have just determined how to operate, we will now talk about the ship and the furnace, how and with what they must be made. When nature cooks metals in mines with natural fire, it can only do so by using a vessel suitable for cooking. We propose to imitate nature in the regime of fire, so let us imitate it also for the ship. Let’s look at where the metals are made. We see at first manifestly in a mine, that under the mountain Ilyadu fire, producing an equal heat, whose nature is to ascend incessantly. By rising it dries and coagulates the thick and coarse water, contained in the bowels of the earth, and transforms it into Mercury. The unctuous mineral parts of the earth are cooked, gathered in the veins of the earth and flowing through the mountain, they generate Sulfur. As can be seen in the veins of the mines, Sulphur born from the smooth parts of the earth meets Mercury. Then the coagulation of the metallic water takes place. The heat continues to act in the mountain, the different metals appear after a very long time. We observe a constant temperature in the mines, we can conclude that the mountain which contains mines is perfectly closed on all sides by rocks because, if the heat could escape; per, metals would never be born. If, then, we wish to imitate nature, we must absolutely have a furnace like a mine, not by its grandeur, but by a special disposition, such that the fire placed in the bottom finds no escape when it rises, so that the heat is reverberated on the vase, closed with care, which contains the matter of the Stone. This is why Aristotle says in the Light of Light, that Mercury must be cooked in a triple vessel made of very hard glass, or, what is better, of earth possessing the hardness of glass.

sections.h: THE TREASURE OF TREASURES BIOGRAPHICAL NOTE ON PARACELSE
p: Auréole Philippe Theophraste Paracejse Bombast ab Hohenheim, was born in 1493 in Einsiedeln, near Zurich, canton of Schwytz. His father Guillaume, an educated doctor, taught him Latin, medicine and alchemy. The works of Isaac the Dutch, which he read in his youth, gave him a deep love of alchemy. From then on he would not separate medicine from alchemy and it was the union of these two sciences that would characterize the school of paracelsists. His father sent him to finish his studies with Trithèrne, a famous occultist who had a great influence on Paracelsus’s ideas, for he taught him magic and astrology. Having retired to a convent, Paracelsus began to travel, he visited Portugal, Spain, Italy, France, the Netherlands, Saxony, Tyrol, Poland, Moravia, Transylvania, Hungary, and Sweden. Perhaps he was even in the East, as he himself insinuates. He went through cities and villages, caring for the sick, selling remedies, drawing horoscopes, evoking the spirits of others; FIVE TREATIES OF ALChimie

One told him a secret, the other told him a wonderful cure. Paracelsus collected everything, judging, comparing, observing. Thus he acquired his prodigious science, which the scholars of his time did not want to recognize, because it was neither in Galen nor in Hippocrates. In Hungary he entered the service of the Fuggers, bankers, alchemists and metallurgists; he was able to work as he pleased; in their vast laboratories. In i:;26, colampade calls him to Basel to fill the chair of physics and surgery (chemistry, Haller says). But he soon had to leave the city, his violent teaching having attracted enemies. He begins to travel again, caring for princes and greats, prelates and rich bourgeois. He died in 1541 at the hospital in Salzburg.

sections.h: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH OF ALBERT THE GREAT
p: Albert the Great, of the ancient family of the Counts of Bollstadt, was born at Lavingen on the Danube in Swabia (1193). In his childhood he was very unintelligent, but as a result of a vision his mind suddenly developed, and from then on he made rapid progress in all branches of science. Around 1222, he entered the Order of St. Dominic. He taught theology and philosophy in the schools of the Order. It was in Cologne that he distinguished among his pupils St. Thomas Aquinas, they formed a close friendship and came together to Paris. The words of Albert the Great attracted such a crowd of listeners that he was obliged to teach in the public squares one of them has preserved; his name is the place Maubert or Master Albert. In 1248 he returned to Cologne. For ten years he led a peaceful existence in this city favorable to study; provincial of his order, enjoying an unquestioned authority with his contemporaries, aided by his monks in all the work he undertook, not having
To worry about money, how different his existence was from that of Roger Bacon!

In 1259 Albert the Great was appointed Bishop of Regensburg, but he soon renounced the cares of the episcopate, and having resigned his office he returned to the cloister. He died in Cologne in 1280 aged 87.

FROM THE FORMATTING OF METALS IN GENERAL BY SULFUR AND MERCURY. It has been observed that the nature of metals, as we know it, is to be generated in a general way by Sulfur and Mercury. The difference in cooking and digestion alone produces variety in the metallic species. I myself have observed that in one and the same vessel, that is, in the same vein, nature had produced several metals and silver, scattered here and there. We have shown clearly in our Treatise on Minerals that the generation of metals is circular, we pass easily from one to the other following a circle, the neighboring metals have similar properties, that is why silver is more easily changed into orc any other metal.

There is no longer any change in silver but color and weight, which is easy. Because a substance that is already compact increases its weight more easily. And since it contains a yellowish white sulfur, its color will also be easy to transform. The same goes for other metals. Sulfur is, so to speak, their father and Mercury their mother. This is even more true, if it is said that in conjunction the Sulfur represents the sperm of the father and that Mercury represents a coagulated menstruation to form the substance of the embryo. Sulphur alone cannot beget, so the father alone. Just as the male begets of his own substance mixed with menstrual blood, so the Sulfur begets with Mercury, but alone it produces nothing. By this comparison we want to make it understood that the Alchemist must first remove from the metal the specificity given to it by Nature, and then proceed as nature proceeded, with Mercury and Sulfur prepared and purified always following the example of nature.

SULFUR. Sulfur contains three wet principles. The first of these principles is mainly aerial and igneous, it is found in the outer parts of Sulfur, even because of the great volatility of its elements, which fly away easily and consume the bodies with which they come into contact. The second principle is phlegmatic, in other words aqueous, it is immediately placed under the previous one. The third is radical, fixed, adhering to the internal parts. This one alone is general, and one cannot separate it from the others without destroying the whole edifice. The first principle does not resist fire being combusted; it is consumed in fire and calcinates the substance of the metal with which it is heated. So it is not only useless, but also harmful to the goal we propose. The second principle only wets the bodies, it does not generate, nor can it serve us. The third is radical; it penetrates all the particles of matter which owes its essential properties to it. It is necessary to rid the Sulfur of the first two principles so that the subtlety of the third can serve us to make a perfect compound.

Fire is nothing but the steam of Sulfur; steam of Sulfur well purified and sublimated whitens and makes more compact. So skilled alchemists are accustomed to remove from Sulfur its two superfluous principles by acid washings, such as lemon vinegar, sour milk, goat milk, children’s urine. They purify it by leaching, digestion, sublimation. It must finally be corrected by resolution so as to have only a pure substance containing the active, perfectible and near force of the metal. We are in possession of a part of our work.
